pages.text: SYN Business Review explains how REITs work for ordinary savers. Officials declined to comment on whether further changes were planned. Industry groups welcomed the clarity but asked for more investor education. Market participants said the move reflected steady demand from retail and institutional investors. According to the regulator, the distribution rule requires REITs to pay out no less than 80 percent of distributable income.

According to the regulator, rEIT income distributions carry a 15 percent withholding tax for resident investors. Unit prices can fall below the value of the underlying property, which is called a discount. A real estate investment trust owns income-producing property and issues units that trade on the exchange.
